description: WHEN OTHER of 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST at :858-865, the THIRD and last arm of the three-arm EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :836, whose WHEN order - NORMAL at :837, NOTFND at :839, OTHER at :858 - is preserved exactly (gate G30), reached here for a DUPLICATE-KEY condition. The subject of this file is a NEGATIVE, and the negative is counted rather than asserted. app/cbl/COACTVWC.cbl is 941 lines long and contains ZERO occurrences of EXEC CICS WRITE, ZERO of REWRITE, ZERO of EXEC CICS DELETE, ZERO of DFHRESP(DUPREC) and ZERO of DFHRESP(DUPKEY) - all five counted - and the three textual occurrences of UPDATE, at :159, :163 and :165, are the literal names LIT-CARDUPDATEPGM, LIT-CARDUPDATEMAPSET and LIT-CARDUPDATEMAP rather than the UPDATE option of a READ, so there is no read-for-update either. Its only file verbs are the three keyed EXEC CICS READs at :727, :776 and :826. common.FileStatus nonetheless publishes DUPLICATE - '22' in the batch vocabulary, and CICS DUPREC = 14 on a base key or DUPKEY = 15 on an alternate key, both sourced from IBM CICS Transaction Server documentation because DFHBMSCA, DFHAID and DFHATTR are IBM-supplied and absent from this repository (risk R-D) - because the programs that do write need it, and gate G47 asks that each of those outcomes be exercised per repository call site. The honest answer for THIS program is that '22' has no dedicated arm to reach: there is no WRITE, no REWRITE, no DELETE and no read-for-update on which a duplicate is even meaningful, so a duplicate reported against any of the three keyed reads matches neither WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) nor WHEN DFHRESP(NOTFND) and lands in WHEN OTHER, composing the generic file-error message this case pins byte for byte. Asserting that, rather than quietly leaving the outcome undriven, is what stops a later implementer inventing a DFHRESP(DUPREC) branch the COBOL does not have (practice B5). The mechanism is named precisely, because it is NOT the one the outcome is named after. ParityCase.ScreenRequest.forcedOutcomes would accept DUPLICATE by type, but COACTVWCParityTest.forcedSite at :403-411 REFUSES it by name, with the reason 'OK and DUPLICATE require a record an empty dataset has none of' - and that refusal is correct, because forcedOutcomes is keyed by RepositoryOperation, all three of this program's reads are READ, and the site is therefore named by the one dataset the case declares EMPTY, a rule enforced at :412-428 where exactly one is required. An empty dataset has no record to duplicate, so a forced DUPLICATE would be a claim about a program that cannot make one. What is declared instead is outcome OTHER on the read of the empty CUSTDAT dataset at 500 bytes over CVCUS01Y, which is exactly the arm a DUPREC or a DUPKEY would land in, and ForcedOutcome.resp and .resp2 are deliberately NOT declared, because the adapter reads only .outcome at :320-322 and a declared code would be inert and therefore misleading (practice B12). case13 reaches this same arm from the other outcome COACTVWC structurally cannot produce, END_OF_FILE, and its note that it is the only file pinning the arm predates this one; the two now pin it as a pair, for two separately recorded reasons - one a browse outcome in a program with no browse, the other a write outcome in a program with no write - over disjoint data, so neither is a copy of the other. Path. EIBCALEN is 172 - the 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy plus the 12-byte WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA at :213-216 that :288-292 splits out of DFHCOMMAREA - with CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 1 and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM COCRDLIC, so the guard at :282-293 takes its ELSE and copies the inbound area rather than INITIALIZEing it. EIBAID is DFHENTER, which the first arm of app/cpy/CSSTRPFY.cpy - copied at :913 - resolves to the ENTER token, so the invalid-key remap at :306-314 leaves it alone. The main EVALUATE TRUE at :323-383 reaches its THIRD arm, WHEN CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :361, whose WHEN order - PFK03 at :324, ENTER at :353, REENTER at :361, OTHER at :375 - is preserved exactly (gate G30). 2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS takes the ELSE at :632 because the typed ACCTSIDI is neither '*' nor spaces, and 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT, whose :650 defensively SETs FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK on entry, passes the blank guard at :653-662 and the not-numeric-or-zeroes guard at :666-676 and reaches its ELSE at :677-680, where :678 moves CC-ACCT-ID into CDEMO-ACCT-ID and :679 SETs FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID, clearing that entry default. INPUT-ERROR is therefore still false at :364, the arm takes the ELSE at :368-373, and 9000-READ-ACCT, 1000-SEND-MAP and GO TO COMMON-RETURN run in that order - a forward-only GO TO reproduced as a plain return with its evaluation order and fall-through outcome intact (rule R7) - bypassing the trailing IF INPUT-ERROR at :387-392. The two reads before the driven one succeed, which is what proves the outcome is applied to one site rather than to every read. CCXREF holds ONE row, fixture row 29 of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt, whose XREF-ACCT-ID span - offset 25, length 11 per CVACT03Y - is 00000000030; no other case in this folder seeds fewer than three cross-reference rows, so this is also the folder's narrowest seed and its proof that the alternate-key finder needs no neighbours. The EXEC CICS READ at :727 against DATASET('CXACAIX ') with an 11-byte RIDFLD and LENGTH(50) finds it and takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL), where :739 moves XREF-CUST-ID 000000030 into CDEMO-CUST-ID and :740 moves XREF-CARD-NUM 6509230362553816 into CDEMO-CARD-NUM. CXACAIX is a PATH over the CCXREF base cluster, reached through the single CardXrefRepository alternate-key finder and never through a second repository or a second table (gate G45). ACCTDAT holds fixture row 29 of acctdata.txt, which is account 00000000030, so the EXEC CICS READ at :776 against DATASET(LIT-ACCTFILENAME) - the PIC X(8) literal 'ACCTDAT ' of :184-185, trailing space included - with RIDFLD(WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X), KEYLENGTH(11), INTO(ACCOUNT-RECORD) and LENGTH(300) succeeds and :788 SETs FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER, so unlike a case that withholds the account this one has a genuinely read 300-byte record to project. :708 then moves CDEMO-CUST-ID into WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID and the customer read at :826 against DATASET(LIT-CUSTFILENAME) - 'CUSTDAT ' of :188-189 - with RIDFLD(WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X), the PIC X(09) REDEFINES at :76-77 and so NINE bytes rather than eleven, KEYLENGTH(9), INTO(CUSTOMER-RECORD) and LENGTH(500), is the one that fails. Its WHEN OTHER body runs in source order: :859 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE, :860 SET FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK TO TRUE, :861 MOVE 'READ' TO ERROR-OPNAME, :862 MOVE LIT-CUSTFILENAME TO ERROR-FILE, :863 MOVE WS-RESP-CD TO ERROR-RESP, :864 MOVE WS-REAS-CD TO ERROR-RESP2, :865 MOVE WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE TO WS-RETURN-MSG. There is no IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF guard on this arm, unlike the NOTFND arm's :845, and the WS-LONG-MSG alias at :866 and the PERFORM SEND-LONG-TEXT at :867 both stay commented out as they are in the source (practice B5). The guard that follows 9400 at :713-715, IF DID-NOT-FIND-CUST-IN-CUSTDAT GO TO 9000-READ-ACCT-EXIT, is DEAD - the only SET that would raise that 88-level is commented out at :842 - and it is immaterial because 9400 is the last read in the paragraph, so nothing observable follows either way; it is recorded rather than tidied (practice B5). The message is arithmetic, not prose. WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE is declared at :86-105 as nine items - FILLER X(12) 'File Error: ', ERROR-OPNAME X(8), FILLER X(4) ' on ', ERROR-FILE X(9), FILLER X(15) ' returned RESP ', ERROR-RESP X(10), FILLER X(7) ',RESP2 ', ERROR-RESP2 X(10) and a trailing FILLER X(5) of spaces - which re-sums by hand as 12+8+4+9+15+10+7+10+5 = 80 (practice B11). Two items are filled by cross-width moves whose padding is stated rather than assumed: MOVE 'READ' into PIC X(8) gives READ followed by FOUR spaces, and MOVE the PIC X(8) literal 'CUSTDAT ' into PIC X(9) gives CUSTDAT followed by TWO - seven characters, the literal's own trailing space, and one more gained on the way into the wider receiver. MOVE WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE TO WS-RETURN-MSG then moves 80 characters into the PIC X(75) declared at :117, and a COBOL alphanumeric receiver truncates on the RIGHT, so the five characters discarded are exactly the trailing FILLER X(5) and nothing but padding is lost, which is why this truncation is safe rather than merely tolerated. :532 moves the surviving 75 bytes into ERRMSGO PIC X(78), re-padding by exactly 3, which is why the expected image measures 78 and ends in four spaces: one from ERROR-RESP2's own justification in PIC X(10) and three from the widening. The two response codes are constants rather than case data and cannot drift (practice B7). A forced OTHER on the customer site makes readCustomer at :629-631 answer CustomerRepository.ReadResult.of(PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS), a status carrying no CICS response, so the resolved RESP is FileStatus.RESP_NOT_REPORTED = -1 and renders through FileStatus.respNotReportedImage as NINE '*' characters left justified in PIC X(10) rather than as a number - so that 'no code was reported' can never be read as the code zero, which is DFHRESP(NORMAL) and would mean success - while the reason code has none to report either and renders as nine zeros. The screen follows from the two flags, and the flag NOT set matters as much as the one that was. 1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS takes its ELSE at :464 because EIBCALEN is 172, and with FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK false :468 echoes the typed CC-ACCT-ID into ACCTSIDO. FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER satisfies the ordered OR at :471-472, so the ten account items at :473-490 are projected from the real record: ACSTTUSO Y; the three PIC X(10) dates 2011-08-26, 2024-06-27 and 2024-06-27 from ACCT-OPEN-DATE, from ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE carrying CVACT01Y's own misspelling verbatim, and from ACCT-REISSUE-DATE; ACCT-GROUP-ID as ten spaces; and the five PIC S9(10)V99 amounts through PIC +ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ.99 at width 15 each - '+          2.00' from the stored image 00000000020{ whose trailing overpunch is a digit and a sign in one byte, '+        120.00' from 00000001200{, '+         93.00' from 00000000930{, and '+           .00' for both cycle amounts - with the sign always emitted, the integer positions Z-suppressed to spaces and the commas they would have preceded blanked along with them, only nine integer positions against a ten-digit source so a tenth digit would truncate on the LEFT, and the two decimal digits still present because the mask ends .99 and not .ZZ. FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is never set, so the IF at :493 is skipped and all EIGHTEEN customer items stay LOW-VALUES - x'00', not spaces and not an edited zero - which is the proof that the customer read failed rather than returned a blank record, and the hyphenating STRING at :496-504 that replaced the direct MOVE CUST-SSN commented out at :495 never runs. 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS moves DFHBMFSE into ACCTSIDA at :543 and DFHDFCOL into ACCTSIDC at :555 and then declines to change it: the IF FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK at :557-559 does NOT fire, because this arm set FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK at :860 - the CUSTOMER flag, not the account flag that 9200 and 9300 set - while 2210's ELSE had already set FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID, and the blank-and-REENTER pair at :561-565 that would add the asterisk does not fire either. So NO DFHRED is applied and NO '*' appears anywhere on this screen even though a file error is displayed on it. That is not an omission: it is gate G38 in its negative form and the counterpart to the positive proof case05 makes. The DFHDFCOL and DFHRED mnemonics both come from common.BmsAttributes, and the highlight is applied inline at :556-565 because COACTVWC does not copy CSSETATY, so common.FieldAttributeSetter is reached only through the account-filter flag this case leaves valid. The cursor EVALUATE TRUE at :546-552 has three arms whose bodies are identical - FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK, FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK and WHEN OTHER all MOVE -1 TO ACCTSIDL - and they are preserved as three rather than collapsed into one (practice B5), which is why cursorField is ACCTSIDL. INFOMSGC is DFHNEUTR rather than the DFHBMDAR of :568 because :528-530 flipped WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE, set at :689, to WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT before :567 tested it, which is also why INFOMSGO carries the prompt of :113-114 - a literal of exactly 40 characters, counted, which fills WS-INFO-MSG PIC X(40) with no padding of its own and then gains five trailing spaces on the way into INFOMSGO PIC X(45). 1400-SEND-SCREEN moves LIT-THISMAPSET and LIT-THISMAP at :579-580 and SETs CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :581, so the reply names COACTVW, CACTVWA and context 1, CDEMO-LAST-MAP and CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET being the PIC X(7) items they are; CDEMO-CUST-ID and CDEMO-CARD-NUM are populated because the NORMAL arm at :739-740 ran first; and the whole conversation - the AID, the commarea and the screen values - travels in the payload with no server-side session state whatsoever (gate G37, rule R6). The operator here is a regular user rather than an administrator, which no other painting case in this folder declares: CDEMO-USER-TYPE is read nowhere in COACTVWC except the unconditional SET CDEMO-USRTYP-USER at :344 on the PF3 arm, so the file-error path is user-type independent and this case is where that is stated. COACTVWC writes nothing - three keyed reads and no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE anywhere - so expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion rather than an absence of interest, and both seeded rows are pinned unchanged on the final-state channel field for field AND as whole images at their declared widths of 50 and 300, with FILLER present and space-filled, 14 bytes on the cross-reference record and 178 on the account record (gates G19 and G21). There is no CUSTDAT row to pin because that read failed and that dataset holds none; CUSTDAT is pinned instead at zero rows and 500 bytes, because an empty dataset is still a fixed-width one. expectedReturnCode is 0: an online WHEN OTHER builds a message and paints a screen, and COACTVWC contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' at all - zero occurrences, counted - so gate G35 does not apply and neither an abend nor a non-zero status is asserted anywhere. expectedMessages is empty because the text is PAINTED into ERRMSGO and the message channel records only the SEND TEXT of SEND-PLAIN-TEXT at :877-887, which this path does not reach. The unit is reached as a plain Java object, AccountViewController constructed through its four-argument constructor with three fixture-backed repository stubs and a fixed clock, with no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container and no HTTP in the path (gate G51). Provenance: every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED from app/cbl/COACTVWC.cbl, from the 300-byte CVACT01Y and 50-byte CVACT03Y layouts including their FILLER spans, from the 500-byte CVCUS01Y width, from the xxxI PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COACTVW.CPY, from the CICS file names in app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD and from the real app/data/ASCII fixtures - and none of it was captured from, recorded against or replayed from a live COBOL execution, which this environment cannot perform (risk R-A). The images are US-ASCII and never a platform default (practice B8); the clock is pinned at 2022-07-19T23:15:58 so CURDATEO is 07/19/22 and CURTIMEO is 23:15:58 (practice B7); TITLE01O comes from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:19 and TITLE02O from its ACTIVE :22 with :21 commented out, neither of them CCDA-THANK-YOU at :23, which is a different field of a different width; and the cross-reference row is seeded at the fixture's own 36 bytes and padded to the 50 CVACT03Y declares by the declared normalisation, this being the one fixture in the repository that does not match its copybook (gate G16, risk R-F). review_rules reports that no user rules were provided for this project, so no user rule governs this file; its absence is not licence to lower the bar, and the enterprise practices B1 through B12 bind in their place.
